correctness.rationale: The pure order EF argument is sound. For a comparable strict pair P<Q, an atom below Q but not P gives (I,L) when P is not bottom; the coatom dual gives (G,I). A pair separated by Q supplies an atom incomparable to both if P is interior and Q is not top. In the incomparable case, meet/join supply the two common strict bounds. The pairs needed for the asymmetric cases come from an atom below exactly one partition or a coatom above exactly one, with strictness controlled by its rank or corank. A pair separated by both exists: otherwise every pair crossing P-blocks would lie in a Q-block, and transitivity would make Q top. Its atom is incomparable to both. This checks the non-chain entries of the extension table. At n≥5 each interior point has an incomparable atom, coatom and middle rank-two point: for an atom pick a triple disjoint from its defining pair, at rank two pick a different rank-two point, and at higher rank merge a triple crossing its blocks. Comparable extension signatures only see clipped height/corank at 3, and the ability to have strict chains of one, two or three steps on each side recovers them; third-point signatures determine the rank-two pointed types by the EF recursion. Since h+c=n−1, the clipped pairs saturate at n=7. The two inner witnesses in the three-step pointed chain test sit in separate branches, so the rank-three separation sentences give all six boundaries and cannot be mistaken for four nested quantifiers. B₇=877 is a minimum within the family only.
